description.value: The study investigated effects of GRIN2C and GRIK1 risk alleles on alcohol cue-induced neural activation and task-related functional connectivity in alcohol-dependent patients, including associations with craving and relapse.

spans.text: The current study investigates genotype effects of four SNPs in glutamatergic neurotransmission genes on alcohol cue-induced neural response and task-related connectivity between ACC, VS and other brain regions, as well as associations with craving and time to first relapse.

value: We expected to detect increased cue-reactivity in risk allele carriers in areas of the brain that demonstrated altered glutamate levels in alcohol dependent patients, such as the ACC, the VS and frontal areas.
We hypothesized that cue-induced brain activation is associated with craving for alcohol and time to first relapse.

description.value: Observational study of alcohol-dependent patients with genotype comparisons and three-month follow-up.

value: Carriers of the risk allele in the GRIK1 gene showed significantly higher activation than homozygous carriers of the protective allele in lateral and medial frontal clusters encompassing the prefrontal and orbitofrontal cortices.
Neural activation in the medial orbitofrontal and prefrontal cortices was positively correlated with subjective craving and predicted time to first relapse.

spans.text: The cue-reactivity fMRI task implemented in the current study was used and validated in previous studies (Vollstadt-Klein et al.
Scanning was performed using a 3T-whole-body-tomograph (MAGNETOM Trio, Siemens, Erlangen, Germany).
T2*-weighted echo-planar images (EPI) were acquired in transversal orientation of 30° clockwise to the anterior commissure-posterior commissure line covering the whole brain.

Imaging parameters were repetition time (TR) = 2.41 seconds, echo time (TE) = 25 ms, flip angle = 80°, 42 slices, slice thickness = 2 mm, 1 mm gap, voxel dimensions 3 × 3 × 3 mm 3 , FOV = 192 × 192 mm 2 , 64 × 64 in-plane resolution.
